---
applyTo: '**/src/locales/**,**/src/**/*.jsx,**/src/**/*.js'
---
# Internationalization (i18n) Guidelines

## Overview
Ancestree uses a static file-based i18n system with React Context. All user-facing text is stored in locale files and accessed via translation hooks.

## Architecture

### File Structure
```
ancestree-app/src/locales/
├── LanguageContext.jsx   # React context, provider, and hooks
├── index.js              # Exports and language configuration
├── de.js                 # German translations (PRIMARY/SOURCE)
└── en.js                 # English translations
```

### Key Components
- **LanguageContext.jsx** - Provides `LanguageProvider`, `useLanguage`, `useTranslation`, `useTranslations` hooks
- **de.js** - German locale file (PRIMARY SOURCE OF TRUTH)
- **en.js** - English locale file (translations of de.js)
- **index.js** - Exports locales and hooks, configures available languages

## CRITICAL: Translation Workflow

### German is the Source Language
**ALWAYS add new text to `de.js` FIRST**, then translate to other language files.

**Workflow for adding new UI text:**
1. Add the new key and German text to `src/locales/de.js`
2. Add the corresponding English translation to `src/locales/en.js`
3. Use the translation in your component via `useTranslation` hook

**Example - Adding a new button label:**
```javascript
// Step 1: Add to de.js
export const de = {
  // ...existing keys
  ui: {
    // ...existing ui keys
    myNewFeature: {
      buttonLabel: 'Neue Aktion',  // German first!
      successMessage: 'Erfolgreich gespeichert',
    }
  }
};

// Step 2: Add to en.js (same structure, English text)
export const en = {
  // ...existing keys
  ui: {
    // ...existing ui keys
    myNewFeature: {
      buttonLabel: 'New Action',
      successMessage: 'Successfully saved',
    }
  }
};
```

### Using Translations in Components

**Standard pattern for functional components:**
```jsx
import { useTranslation } from './locales/LanguageContext';

function MyComponent() {
  const { t } = useTranslation();
  
  return (
    <div>
      <h1>{t.header.title}</h1>
      <button>{t.ui.myNewFeature.buttonLabel}</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

**For components that need language switching:**
```jsx
import { useLanguage } from './locales/LanguageContext';

function LanguageAwareComponent() {
  const { language, setLanguage, translations } = useLanguage();
  
  return (
    <select value={language} onChange={(e) => setLanguage(e.target.value)}>
      <option value="de">Deutsch</option>
      <option value="en">English</option>
    </select>
  );
}
```

### Memoized Components
For `React.memo` components that can't use hooks directly, pass translations as props:

```jsx
// Parent component
const { t } = useTranslation();
return <MemoizedChild translations={t.ui.childSection} />;

// Memoized child
const MemoizedChild = React.memo(({ translations }) => {
  return <span>{translations.label}</span>;
});
```

## Locale File Structure

Each locale file must export an object with this structure:
```javascript
export const de = {
  _meta: {
    code: 'de',           // Language code (must match key in locales object)
    name: 'Deutsch',      // Display name for language picker
    flag: '🇩🇪'           // Flag emoji for UI
  },
  header: { /* header translations */ },
  ui: {
    tabs: { /* tab labels */ },
    editor: { /* node editor labels */ },
    sidebar: { /* sidebar translations */ },
    imageGallery: { /* image gallery translations */ },
    // ... other UI sections
  },
  // ... other top-level sections
};
```

## Adding a New Language

1. **Create the locale file** (e.g., `src/locales/fr.js`):
   ```javascript
   // Copy structure from de.js, translate all values
   export const fr = {
     _meta: {
       code: 'fr',
       name: 'Français',
       flag: '🇫🇷'
     },
     // ... translate all keys from de.js
   };
   ```

2. **Register in index.js**:
   ```javascript
   import { fr } from './fr';
   
   export const locales = {
     de,
     en,
     fr,  // Add here
   };
   
   export { de, en, fr };  // Add to exports
   ```

3. **The language will automatically appear** in `LanguagePicker` component

## Translation Key Conventions

### Naming Patterns
- Use **camelCase** for all keys
- Group related translations under descriptive parent keys
- Use specific, descriptive names (not generic like `text1`, `label2`)

**Good:**
```javascript
ui: {
  nodeEditor: {
    nameLabel: 'Name',
    saveButton: 'Speichern',
    deleteConfirmation: 'Möchten Sie diese Person wirklich löschen?'
  }
}
```

**Bad:**
```javascript
ui: {
  label1: 'Name',
  btn: 'Speichern',
  msg: 'Möchten Sie diese Person wirklich löschen?'
}
```

### Organizing New Features
When adding a new feature, create a dedicated section:
```javascript
ui: {
  existingFeature: { /* ... */ },
  
  // New feature gets its own section
  newFeatureName: {
    title: 'Feature Titel',
    description: 'Beschreibung des Features',
    actions: {
      save: 'Speichern',
      cancel: 'Abbrechen'
    },
    messages: {
      success: 'Erfolgreich!',
      error: 'Ein Fehler ist aufgetreten'
    }
  }
}
```

## Fallback Behavior

- **Default language**: German (`de`)
- **Missing translations**: Falls back to German text
- **Missing keys**: Returns the key path as string and logs a warning

```javascript
// If en.js is missing a key, German text is used
t.ui.someNewKey  // Returns German value if English missing
```

## Session Persistence

- Language preference is stored in `sessionStorage` under key `ancestree-language`
- Persists during browser session but resets on new session
- Default language (German) is used if no preference stored

## DO NOT

- ❌ Hardcode user-facing text in components
- ❌ Add English text to `de.js` (German only!)
- ❌ Add text to `en.js` without corresponding `de.js` entry
- ❌ Use different key structures between locale files
- ❌ Import from `config.js` for new code (legacy - use `useTranslation`)

## DO

- ✅ Add new text to `de.js` first, then translate to `en.js`
- ✅ Use `useTranslation` hook in all new components
- ✅ Keep locale file structures identical across all languages
- ✅ Use descriptive, hierarchical key names
- ✅ Test language switching after adding new translations
